description: A curated collection of free and publicly available Open Source Threat Intelligence feeds, covering IP addresses, domains, URLs, file hashes, CVEs, and other Indicators of Compromise (IOCs) for threat hunting, detection, and security research.

#
Open-Source Threat Intelligence Feeds
[![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/Bert-JanP/Open-Source-Threat-Intel-Feeds?style=social)](https://github.com/Bert-JanP/Open-Source-Threat-Intel-Feeds/stargazers) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/Bert-JanP/Open-Source-Threat-Intel-Feeds)](./LICENSE) [![Feeds](https://img.shields.io/badge/feeds-165-blue)](./ThreatIntelFeeds.csv) [![Tweet](https://img.shields.io/twitter/url?url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2FBert-JanP%2FOpen-Source-Threat-Intel-Feeds&style=social)](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Open%20Source%20Threat%20Intel%20Feeds%20for%20threat%20hunting&url=https://github.com/Bert-JanP/Open-Source-Threat-Intel-Feeds) **A curated, community-maintained catalog of public threat intelligence and IOC feeds.**
Browse the sources directly, import the catalog into a threat hunting workflow, or use it to enrich detections in your SIEM and EDR platform. ## Table of contents - [Quick start](#quick-start) - [Catalog at a glance](#catalog-at-a-glance) - [Use feeds in KQL](#use-feeds-in-kql) - [Contribute](#contribute) - [Feed sources](#feed-sources) ## Quick start There are three ways to use this repository: | Goal | Resource | | --- | --- | | Browse every source | [ThreatIntelFeeds.csv](./ThreatIntelFeeds.csv) | | Find a provider or feed | [Feed sources](#feed-sources) at the bottom of this README | | Import feeds into Microsoft Sentinel or Defender XDR | Follow the [KQL example](#use-feeds-in-kql) | The CSV is semicolon-delimited and uses this schema: ```text Vendor;Description;Category;Url;FeedStatus ``` > [!IMPORTANT] > Public availability does not automatically mean a feed can be used for every purpose. Feed-specific terms, retention, attribution, redistribution, and commercial-use conditions must be checked before production use. The catalog is provided as-is. ## Catalog at a glance The catalog currently contains **170 feed entries** across the following indicator categories: | Category | Count | | --- | --- | | DNS | 23 | | IP | 83 | | MD5 | 13 | | SHA1 | 5 | | SHA256 | 11 | | SSL | 1 | | URL | 26 | | CVEID | 5 | | RANSOMWARELEAK | 1 | | JA3 | 1 | | NamePipe | 1 | Supported categories are: `SSL`, `IP`, `DNS`, `URL`, `MD5`, `SHA1`, `SHA256`, `CVEID`, `RANSOMWARELEAK`, `JA3`, and `NamePipe`. ## Use feeds in KQL Microsoft Sentinel and Microsoft 365 Defender support the [`externaldata` operator](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-explorer/kusto/query/externaldata-operator). Use it to turn a public CSV or TXT feed into a table that can be joined against network, authentication, file, or vulnerability telemetry. ```kusto let C2IntelFeeds = externaldata(IP:string, IOC:string) [ @"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/drb-ra/C2IntelFeeds/master/feeds/IPC2s-30day.csv" ] with (format="csv", ignoreFirstRecord=true); C2IntelFeeds | take 100 ``` The following example compares remote IP telemetry with a C2 feed and adds geolocation context: ```kusto let C2IntelFeeds = externaldata(IP:string, IOC:string) [ @"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/drb-ra/C2IntelFeeds/master/feeds/IPC2s-30day.csv" ] with (format="csv", ignoreFirstRecord=true); DeviceNetworkEvents | where RemoteIP in (C2IntelFeeds | project IP) | join kind=inner C2IntelFeeds on $left.RemoteIP == $right.IP | extend GeoIPInfo = geo_info_from_ip_address(RemoteIP) | extend country = tostring(parse_json(GeoIPInfo).country), state = tostring(parse_json(GeoIPInfo).state), city = tostring(parse_json(GeoIPInfo).city) | project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, IOC ``` ![MDE external data example](./Img/MDEExternalData.png "External data collected in Advanced Hunting") For more ready-to-run examples, see the [KQL Hunting Queries and Detection Rules](https://github.com/Bert-JanP/Hunting-Queries-Detection-Rules/tree/main/Threat%20Hunting). ## Contribute Community contributions keep this catalog useful and current. 1. Add or update the source under the matching provider in the [feed source list](#feed-sources). 2. Add the vendor, description, category, URL, and status to [ThreatIntelFeeds.csv](./ThreatIntelFeeds.csv). 3. Use a category from `valid_categories` in [Validator.py](./Scripts/Validator.py). 4. Prefer sources that are directly accessible without accounts or API keys. 5. Run the CSV validator from the `Scripts` directory: ```powershell cd Scripts python Validator.py ``` 6. Refresh the statistics table from the `Scripts` directory when categories change: ```powershell cd Scripts python GenerateTableStatistics.py ``` ## Feed sources ⚠️ **Terms of Service:** Before using any feed, validate the provider's current Terms of Service and usage restrictions yourself.
